items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Hymie Schertzer was playing lead alto then. He was good friends with Benny. He went up to Benny and said, “Why did you fire that kid? That kid is sensational.”

ctx.x: No, he didn’t. All he said was, “You’ve got the job, and I’ll see you Thursday on the train.” Now the big question came: how am I going to tell Ted FioRito? Candy Candido and the rest of the band found out about it. They said, “Go to Benny. We’ll explain to Ted later on what happened.” I said, “Yeah, but I can’t do that. Let me at least tell Ted.” They said, “No. He’s a bull-headed Italian. He’s not going to go for it.” They said, “You go on ahead. We’ll fix it up.” So Ted really got mad, but later on, he…

“Look kid. I didn’t want to stand in your way.” Benny Goodman was hot in those days. Sing, Sing, Sing and all that. So I went to New York with Benny. My first gig in New York was at the New Yorker Hotel. While we played with the band there, we had a tremendous ice show to play. The band had to play the ice show. The drum book was three inches thick. I had to play tympani cues, xylophone, and drum set. That was my meat. I could breeze through that. All the ice skaters said, “Keep him with you all the time.” But…
So you went back to play with him after you got back? Your dad told you, “Benny Goodman wants you in place”?
